author: reek
body: `GopHid` -- the decoder that turns an 8-byte boot report into scancodes -- has a test (`hid-decode`). `GopUsbKbd`, which is the code that actually has to get that report off an interrupt endpoint, has never been run by anything: not by a battery, not under the emulator. It is the half that fails on real hardware, and it is the half nobody could see.

author: reek
body: What each line proves. `connect` says the port walk, the descriptor walk, SET_CONFIGURATION, SET_PROTOCOL, SET_IDLE and Configure Endpoint all completed -- the driver got as far on the emulator as it did on the metal. `dci` says which endpoint it settled on. `armed` and `code` say whether a transfer was queued and whether a completion came back, which is precisely where the real machine produced nothing at all.

author: reek
body: Pump once to arm a transfer, then once more to check for a completion. The phase cell after each call says which branch the pump took, so a driver that never leaves idle is distinguishable from one that arms and hears nothing back -- two different failures that look identical from the outside.
